ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First look at the image: In the diagram, A is at the lower left, B is at the upper left, and C is on the right; BC is marked as a meridian, AB is a certain parallel, AC is the oblique terminator line connecting A to C, beside point C is marked “(0°,30°W)”, and on the left there is also an arrow for “direction of rotation”. Then combine the question stem: The local time at point A is 12 o'clock and the sun is on the horizon, indicating that point A is located on the terminator line. Then reason: From the indicated direction of rotation and the position of the terminator line, AC can be judged to be the evening line, so the local time at point C is 18 o'clock. The longitude of point C is 30°W, so the 12 o'clock meridian that differs from point C by 6 hours is 90° to its west, namely 120°W. The 12 o'clock meridian is the center of the daylight range on the equator, with 90° on each side of the meridian, so the daylight range on the equator is 150°E—30°W. Then look at the condition “with the same date as Beijing”: Beijing is approximately at 120°E, and if the 0 o'clock meridian is at 60°E, then the range with the same date as Beijing is 60°E—180°. Taking the intersection of the daylight range and the same-date range gives 150°E—180°.
